settings.title: Settings
settings.restoreDefaultHint: Puts back the original value, the one from before any change
settings.accountDescription: API credentials, encrypted by the system keychain.
settings.generationDescription: Generation queue and default models, per family.
settings.mediaDescription: Preparation of imported files: proxies and waveforms.
settings.dictationDescription: Speaking a text instead of typing it. Everything happens on this computer: nothing you say is sent anywhere.

theme.title: Theme
theme.help: Picks the colours of the whole application. The dark theme rests the eyes over a long session in a dimly lit room; the light one reads better in broad daylight. “System” follows your computer's own setting and switches on its own, for instance when evening comes.

density.title: Density
density.help: Sets how big the buttons are and how tall the rows sit. “Compact” fits more on screen; “Comfortable” leaves more air between things, which makes them easier to aim at with a mouse.

concurrentJobs.title: Concurrent generations
concurrentJobs.help: How many creations work at the same time. The higher it is, the more you can start at once — but each may take longer to come back, and the service can turn away the ones arriving on top. Three is a good balance.

captionArrivals.title: Describe fetched assets
captionArrivals.help: Automatically name a picture that arrives without a useful name. Spends creative units.

maxRetries.title: Max retries
maxRetries.help: When a generation fails because the network dropped or a server was busy, the application tries again on its own. This number says how many times before giving up. At 0 it never tries twice. An invalid API key is never retried: trying again would not fix it.

ffmpegPath.title: Path to ffmpeg
ffmpegPath.help: Where to find an ffmpeg to use instead of the one shipped with the application. Leave empty unless you insist on your own.

dictationEnabled.title: Enable dictation
dictationEnabled.help: Offers a microphone button beside text fields, and puts the listening shortcut into service. Switched off, dictation loads nothing and never asks for microphone access.

dictationMode.title: How it is triggered
dictationMode.help: “Hold” listens for as long as you keep the shortcut pressed and stops the moment you let go: it is the safest, since the microphone is never left open by mistake. “Toggle” starts on the first press and stops on the next, which rests the hand over a long dictation.

dictationSilence.title: Silence that ends a sentence
dictationSilence.help: How much quiet, in milliseconds, before what you have just said counts as finished and gets transcribed. Raise it if your sentences are cut in half because you pause to think.

dictationPreview.title: Preview while you speak
dictationPreview.help: How long, in milliseconds, between two previews of the text being spoken. The model does not write as the words come: every preview reads back everything said since the sentence began, and so costs computation. Set it to 0 to show only the settled text of each sentence.

dictationThreads.title: Compute threads
dictationThreads.help: How many cores recognition may occupy. Higher is faster up to a point, but every thread is a core taken away from the rest of the application.

dictationIdleUnload.title: Free the memory after
dictationIdleUnload.help: Minutes without dictating before the model is unloaded, returning around 700 MB of memory. It loads itself again on the next dictation, which takes a few seconds. Set it to 0 to keep it resident.

dictationModelFolder.title: Model folder
dictationModelFolder.help: Where to find a recognition model already on this disk, to use instead of the one the application downloads. Leave empty in the normal case.

settings.ffmpegFound: ffmpeg is available: proxies and waveforms will be prepared.
settings.ffmpegMissing: ffmpeg is still not found. Importing works, without proxy or waveform.

accent.title: Accent colour
accent.help: The colour that marks what is selected or under way: the outline of the active panel, the timeline playhead, the frame around a selection. It changes nothing about what you make, only how the application shows you where you are. Leave it be to keep the theme's own.

fontScale.title: Text size
fontScale.help: Makes every text in the application bigger or smaller at once. 1 is the size it was drawn at; above that words get larger and less fits on screen; below, the opposite. Buttons keep their size: density is what handles those.

reduceMotion.title: Limit animations
reduceMotion.help: Turns off the small movements of the interface: panels appear at once instead of sliding in. Useful if animation tires you or makes you queasy, and on a slower machine where it stutters.

settings.generalDescription: The application's language, and what it does when it opens.

language.title: Language
language.help: The language of every text in the application: menus, buttons, messages. “System” follows your computer's own language. The change is immediate — there is nothing to relaunch. It leaves your projects, and anything you write in them, alone.

startup.title: On opening
startup.help: What the application does when you launch it. “Reopen the last project” puts you back where you left off. “Open nothing” starts on an empty window, which is quicker and calmer if you juggle a lot of projects.

home.title: Show the home screen
home.help: The full-width screen the studio opens on: your projects, what you were working on, what is running, and what the models can do. Turn it off to go straight to the workspace you left. Which sections it shows, and in which order, is set on the home itself.

settings.discardTitle: Some settings have not been applied
settings.discardBody: You changed settings without applying them. What would you like to do?
settings.shortcutsDescription: The keys that trigger each action. Click a key to replace it.
settings.shortcutConflict: Two actions are fighting over this key: only one will answer.
settings.chordFree: No action uses this key: it is free.
settings.spacesDescription: What only makes sense inside one space: the 3D view, the edit, the image.
settings.requires: Has no effect while “{{setting}}” is off.

showGrid.title: Show the grid
showGrid.help: The squared floor of the 3D view. It is not part of what you are making: it is a landmark for where things are and how high. Hide it to judge an image with nothing around it.

gridSize.title: Grid size
gridSize.help: How far the grid reaches, in metres, and therefore how many squares it has — a square is always one metre. Make it bigger for a wide scene, smaller for a little object sitting near the camera.

flySpeed.title: Fly speed
flySpeed.help: How fast the camera moves when you fly through the 3D view, in metres per second. Too slow and crossing the scene takes ten seconds; too fast and you shoot past it without seeing it.

boostFactor.title: Boost
boostFactor.help: What the speed is multiplied by while you hold the boost key. At 3 you go three times faster — enough to cross a large scene without changing the setting above.

shadowQuality.title: Shadow softness
shadowQuality.help: The grain of a shadow's edge. Hard cuts cleanly and costs the least; Soft smooths the edge. What throws a shadow, on the other hand, is decided object by object in the inspector.

shadowMapSize.title: Shadow detail
shadowMapSize.help: The side, in pixels, of the shadow map each shadow-casting light computes. Doubling it costs four times the memory: 2048 is plenty for a scene of a few objects, 4096 earns its keep when one light covers a whole set.

snapTranslate.title: Move step
snapTranslate.help: How far an object travels in one step while snapping is on, in metres. Snapping itself is switched on from the scene toolbar; this only says how fine it is.

snapRotate.title: Turn step
snapRotate.help: The angle of one step of rotation while snapping is on, in degrees. Rotation steps on from wherever it started: 15° gives twenty-four steps per turn, 90° quarter turns.

snapScale.title: Scale step
snapScale.help: How much the scale moves in one step while snapping is on. What is reachable is the multiples of the step: 0.1 lands exactly on tenths and halves, 0.25 on quarters.

fieldOfView.title: Field of view
fieldOfView.help: How much the camera takes in, in degrees. A narrow angle pulls close and flattens, like a telephoto lens; a wide one shows far more but bends the edges. 60 is close to what an eye sees.

settings.advancedDescription: What is only needed to understand a problem, or to start over.

logLevel.title: Log detail
logLevel.help: How much the application says about what it is doing, in the console. “Nothing” says nothing at all; “Errors” reports only what failed; “Everything” narrates each step, which helps to understand a problem and is chatty the rest of the time.

openSettingsFile.title: Settings file
openSettingsFile.help: Shows where your settings are saved, in the file manager. Useful to copy them before moving to another machine, or to send them to someone helping you.

openDevtools.title: Developer tools
openDevtools.help: Opens the technical console of the embedded browser. It shows the log messages and the errors. For troubleshooting only: nothing in there is needed to use the software.

resetAll.title: Reset everything
resetAll.help: Puts EVERY setting back to a fresh install: theme, language, shortcuts, all of it. Your projects, images and edits are untouched — only the settings are. There is no going back.
resetAll.confirm: Reset every setting? Your projects are untouched, but this cannot be undone.

settings.storageDescription: Where your projects are kept on disk.

projectsFolder.title: Projects folder
projectsFolder.help: The folder the application offers when you create or open a project. It moves nothing: projects already created stay where they are. Leave it empty to start from wherever you last were.

settings.cancelHint: Drops the pending changes, without closing the window
settings.applyHint: Writes the changes now, and leaves the window open
settings.confirmHint: Writes the changes, then closes the window
settings.browseHint: Pick the folder in a system window
settings.findByChordHint: Click, then press a chord: the list keeps only what uses it
settings.showAllHint: Clears the filter and shows every shortcut again
settings.captureHint: Click, then press the chord to assign
settings.sectionHint: Shows the settings of this section
settings.sectionStagedHint: This section has changes that were not applied
settings.searchSectionHint: Opens the whole section, rather than the one result
settings.searchResultHint: Goes to the setting, in the section it belongs to

skybox.empty: Open a skybox to grade it.
skybox.noSource: No skybox yet. Generate one or drop an equirectangular panorama.

projectNew.title: New project
projectNew.help: Creates an empty project and opens it. A project is the folder holding everything you make: the images, the videos, the sounds, and how they are arranged.

projectOpen.title: Open project
projectOpen.help: Picks a project already on your disk and opens it in place of the current one. The open project is saved as you go, so there is nothing to save first.

documentSave.title: Save document
documentSave.help: Writes the document in front into the project. A 3D scene lives in the window until it is saved: the tab carries a dot for as long as what is on screen is not what is on disk.

layoutReset.title: Reset layout
layoutReset.help: Puts the panels back where they started. Useful once the windows have been dragged all over and nothing is where you expect. Your work is untouched.

appSettings.title: Settings
appSettings.help: Opens the settings window — this one: the language, the colours, the account, the shortcuts, and everything else that is adjustable.

appDictate.title: Dictate
appDictate.help: Listens to the microphone and writes what you say at the caret, in the field you are in. Held down by default: speak, let go, the text appears.

windowFullScreen.title: Full screen
windowFullScreen.help: Gives the window the whole screen, with no bar and no border, to work with nothing around it.

spacesMoveLeft.title: Move the space left
spacesMoveLeft.help: Shifts the focused space one place to the left in the top bar. The order you settle on is kept from one session to the next.

spacesMoveRight.title: Move the space right
spacesMoveRight.help: Shifts the focused space one place to the right in the top bar. The order you settle on is kept from one session to the next.

sceneSelect.title: Select
sceneSelect.help: The plain tool: click an object in the scene to choose it, without doing anything to it. It is the one you come back to between manipulations.

sceneTranslate.title: Move
sceneTranslate.help: Drags the chosen object from one place to another, by pulling the coloured arrows — one per direction.

sceneRotate.title: Rotate
sceneRotate.help: Turns the chosen object on itself, by pulling the coloured rings — one per axis.

sceneScale.title: Scale
sceneScale.help: Makes the chosen object bigger or smaller, by pulling its handles. Holding Shift keeps its proportions.

sceneFrame.title: Frame selection
sceneFrame.help: Brings the camera close enough that the chosen object fills the view. Handy when you are lost, or when an object is tiny.

sceneSnap.title: Snapping
sceneSnap.help: Moves the handles in regular steps instead of leaving them free. Handy for laying objects out in line. How fine the steps are is set in the 3D space preferences.

sceneSpace.title: Local frame
sceneSpace.help: Lines the handles up with the object's own orientation rather than the world's. On a turned object, that is what lets you move it “towards its front” rather than north.

sceneProjection.title: Projection
sceneProjection.help: Switches between perspective, where receding lines converge, and orthographic projection, where parallels stay parallel. That is what lets an alignment be judged by eye.

sceneDisplay.title: Display
sceneDisplay.help: Cycles what the viewport draws: the surfaces, their edges alone, or both together. The button's menu picks one directly.

sceneGroup.title: Group
sceneGroup.help: Files the selected objects under one group. Moving the group moves them all, and ⌘Z takes the grouping back.

sceneDuplicate.title: Duplicate
sceneDuplicate.help: Puts a copy of the selection under the same parent and at the very same place, then selects it. A group duplicates whole, with everything hanging from it.

sceneCopy.title: Copy
sceneCopy.help: Holds on to the selection so it can be pasted, here or in another scene. This is the studio's own clipboard: it leaves the system one alone.

sceneCut.title: Cut
sceneCut.help: Holds on to the selection and takes it out of the scene. ⌘Z brings it back.

scenePaste.title: Paste
scenePaste.help: Puts what was copied into the scene in front, and selects it. Pasting twice makes two separate copies.

sceneDelete.title: Delete
sceneDelete.help: Removes everything selected from the scene. Nothing is lost for good: ⌘Z brings it back.

undo.title: Undo
undo.help: Takes back the last thing you did in this document. Each document has its own stack: undo acts on the tab in front, not on the others.

redo.title: Redo
redo.help: Does again what you have just undone. Handy after undoing once too often.

sequencePlayPause.title: Play / Pause
sequencePlayPause.help: Starts playing the edit, or stops it where it is. Starting again picks up where you left off.

sequenceSplit.title: Split clip
sequenceSplit.help: Cuts the clip in two where the playhead sits, so each half can be handled on its own.

sequenceDelete.title: Delete clip
sequenceDelete.help: Removes the chosen clip from the edit. The original file stays in your assets.

sequenceZoomIn.title: Zoom in
sequenceZoomIn.help: Spreads the edit out to see detail: clips get wider and are easier to aim at.

sequenceZoomOut.title: Zoom out
sequenceZoomOut.help: Draws the edit together to see more of it at once, at the cost of the detail.

sequenceFit.title: Fit to view
sequenceFit.help: Sets the zoom so the whole edit fits on screen, end to end.

sequenceStart.title: Go to start
sequenceStart.help: Brings the playhead right back to the beginning of the edit, moving nothing else.

sequenceEnd.title: Go to end
sequenceEnd.help: Sends the playhead right to the end of the edit, past the last clip.

canvasZoomIn.title: Zoom in
canvasZoomIn.help: Magnifies the view one step, around the middle of what is visible. The image itself is untouched — only the way it is looked at.

canvasZoomOut.title: Zoom out
canvasZoomOut.help: Shrinks the view one step, to take in the whole image again.

canvasZoomFit.title: Fit to window
canvasZoomFit.help: Frames the whole image in the panel, with a margin, and never magnifies it past its actual size.

canvasZoomActual.title: Actual size
canvasZoomActual.help: One image pixel per screen pixel: the only scale at which sharpness can be judged.

canvasRulers.title: Rulers
canvasRulers.help: Shows or hides the two graduated rulers, at the top and on the left. Guides are pulled off them.

canvasGuides.title: Guides
canvasGuides.help: Shows or hides the guides laid on the image. Hiding them does not remove them.

canvasClearGuides.title: Clear guides
canvasClearGuides.help: Removes every guide from the image. Undoable, like any other edit.

canvasSnap.title: Snap
canvasSnap.help: Makes what is dragged stick to guides, to the image edges and to its centre, within a few pixels.

canvasDeselect.title: Deselect
canvasDeselect.help: Drop the selected region, so the brush reaches the whole layer again

canvasCropApply.title: Apply the crop
canvasCropApply.help: Trim the document to the placed frame. ⌘Z gives the frame back, not the pixels

canvasCropCancel.title: Abandon the crop
canvasCropCancel.help: Take the crop frame away without trimming anything at all

canvasMaskFromSelection.title: Make a mask of the selection
canvasMaskFromSelection.help: Hide the armed layer outside the selected region

canvasRegenerate.title: Regenerate the region
canvasRegenerate.help: Ask the model to repaint the masked region of the armed layer

canvasCutout.title: Cut out
canvasCutout.help: Remove the background of the flattened image with the default model

canvasEnlarge.title: Enlarge
canvasEnlarge.help: Raise the definition of the flattened image with the default model

canvasVectorize.title: Vectorize
canvasVectorize.help: Turn the flattened image into paths with the default model

canvasExtend.title: Extend
canvasExtend.help: Ask the model to paint beyond the edges of the flattened image

canvasMergeDown.title: Merge down
canvasMergeDown.help: Join the active layer and the one just below it into one, keeping the lower one's name

canvasFlatten.title: Flatten image
canvasFlatten.help: Reduce the whole stack to a single layer: hidden layers are dropped, not merged

canvasFlipHorizontal.title: Flip horizontal
canvasFlipHorizontal.help: Mirror the whole document left to right, layers included

canvasFlipVertical.title: Flip vertical
canvasFlipVertical.help: Mirror the whole document top to bottom, layers included

canvasRotateCw.title: Rotate clockwise
canvasRotateCw.help: Turn the document a quarter turn to the right: the frame turns with it

canvasRotateCcw.title: Rotate counter-clockwise
canvasRotateCcw.help: Turn the document a quarter turn to the left: the frame turns with it

canvasExport.title: Export the image
canvasExport.help: Write the flattened document to disk, as a PNG

skyboxView.title: Change the view
skyboxView.help: Cycles through the four ways of looking at the sky: immersive, panoramic, cross, faces.

skyboxProbes.title: Light probes
skyboxProbes.help: Shows or hides the witness spheres. A sky is judged by what it lights, not by its own picture.

canvasToolMove.title: Move tool
canvasToolMove.help: Arms the pointer: a drag moves the armed layer, and its grips resize or turn it.

canvasToolHand.title: Hand tool
canvasToolHand.help: Arms the hand: a drag pans the view without touching the document. Holding space does the same without changing tool.

canvasToolScale.title: Scale tool
canvasToolScale.help: Arms scaling: the armed layer's grips resize it, and Shift keeps its proportions.

canvasToolCrop.title: Crop tool
canvasToolCrop.help: Arms the crop frame. Draw a frame, then ⏎ to crop or ⎋ to drop it.

canvasToolSelectRectangle.title: Rectangular selection
canvasToolSelectRectangle.help: Arms the rectangular selection. What is selected bounds the brush, the eraser and the bucket.

canvasToolSelectEllipse.title: Elliptical selection
canvasToolSelectEllipse.help: Arms the elliptical selection: a drag inscribes the ellipse in the rectangle swept, and Shift makes it a circle.

canvasToolSelectLasso.title: Lasso
canvasToolSelectLasso.help: Arms the lasso: the selection follows the hand, freehand.

canvasToolShapeRectangle.title: Rectangle shape
canvasToolShapeRectangle.help: Arms drawing a rectangle on the armed layer; Shift makes it a square.

canvasToolShapeLine.title: Line shape
canvasToolShapeLine.help: Arms drawing a line. Same group as the rectangle, hence its key with Shift added.

canvasToolShapeArrow.title: Arrow shape
canvasToolShapeArrow.help: Arms drawing an arrow, from where the drag began to where the hand lets go.

canvasToolShapeEllipse.title: Ellipse shape
canvasToolShapeEllipse.help: Arms drawing an ellipse on the armed layer; Shift makes it a circle.

canvasToolShapePolygon.title: Polygon shape
canvasToolShapePolygon.help: Arms drawing a regular polygon, whose number of sides is set in the inspector before drawing.

canvasToolShapeStar.title: Star shape
canvasToolShapeStar.help: Arms drawing a star, whose number of points is set in the inspector before drawing.

canvasToolBrush.title: Brush tool
canvasToolBrush.help: Arms the brush, with a softened edge. It paints on the armed layer, bounded by the selection when there is one.

canvasToolPencil.title: Pencil tool
canvasToolPencil.help: Arms the pencil, with a hard edge: the same gesture as the brush, without the softening.

canvasToolText.title: Text tool
canvasToolText.help: Arms text: a click places a caption, whose words are typed in the inspector.

canvasToolEraser.title: Eraser tool
canvasToolEraser.help: Arms the point eraser: it clears where the hand passes, bounded by the selection when there is one.

canvasToolEraserSelection.title: Erase the selection
canvasToolEraserSelection.help: Arms the selection eraser: one click clears everything the selection encloses at once, rather than rubbing it out.

canvasToolFill.title: Paint bucket tool
canvasToolFill.help: Arms the bucket: a click fills the layer, or the selection when there is one.

canvasToolPicker.title: Eyedropper tool
canvasToolPicker.help: Arms the eyedropper: a click takes the colour under the pointer and hands it to the brush.

canvasBrushSmaller.title: Smaller brush
canvasBrushSmaller.help: Narrows the brush, the eraser and the shape stroke by one step of the scale.

canvasBrushLarger.title: Larger brush
canvasBrushLarger.help: Widens the brush, the eraser and the shape stroke by one step of the scale.
